title: an-open-reading-is-not-silently-converted
author: CC
owner: CC builds it; cairn/devices/tester owns the store's write door and the CLI's per-proof isolation read
intention: A standing seal of `open` is a RECORDED CHOICE NOT TO MEASURE, and replacing it with a measured reading is an act that must carry a reason. The store's write door refuses a measured seal landing over a standing `open` unless a reason rides with it, and that reason lands permanently in the record's evidence — the exact shape, and the exact vocabulary, that `unsealing_because` already has for the mirror direction. Beside it, the sweep says out loud when an explicit `--netns` disagrees with what the standing record says, BEFORE it runs, naming the proof and the reading it is about to override.
why: cairn/devices/tester/cli.py:434 returns `netns` on `args.netns` before the standing record is ever read, and prints nothing. Ticket 4431cf2bc625 built the per-proof read at :437 precisely so a sweep would reproduce the isolation each proof was last sealed at instead of flattening the corpus to one answer — and then left the path a hand takes deliberately wide open. The cost is not a wrong reading in one run. Measured end to end on a fixture 2026-09-10: after ONE `cairn test --netns --seal` over a standing `open`, a later PLAIN `cairn test --seal` reproduces `netns` forever, because the per-proof read now finds a measured seal where the deliberate `open` stood. The `open` is unrecoverable from the record, and nothing anywhere says a conversion happened. THE ASYMMETRY IS THE FINDING: the same store raises `SealDowngradeRefused` rather than let a MEASUREMENT be retired without a written reason, and lets a deliberate NON-measurement be retired without one. A guard written for one direction of a two-directional act is half-installed. Law 7: the validation is a record of truth, not a presentation surface, so it is the one place a change with no reason on it may never land quietly. Law 3: `open` is not a weaker measurement, it is the recorded absence of one, and overwriting it destroys the only artifact saying so. AND THE LOSS IS TOTAL, NOT MERELY UNANNOUNCED — measured 2026-09-10 after the cast, from the tester's own charter and then from the corpus: `persist_validation` writes `[record]`, a one-element list, and all 219 validation files across both roots hold exactly ONE record. The store REPLACES; there is no trail. So a conversion does not leave a superseded `open` behind it to be found — after it lands, nothing anywhere on disk has ever said `open` for that proof, and the converted record is indistinguishable from a first seal. That is what makes a reason riding IN the surviving record the only possible remedy: there is no second place to put one.
how: Two edges, one component, no new writer. (1) THE GUARD, at cairn/devices/tester/validation_store.py, beside `SealDowngradeRefused` at :414 and raised at the same site (:668) — before the announce and before the write, so a refused conversion neither prints nor lands. It fires ONLY when a standing record exists AND reads `open` AND the incoming reading is measured; the escape is a reason parameter mirroring `unsealing_because`, riding permanently in the record's evidence. The store is the home rather than the CLI because it is the one door every persisting path passes — cli.py:449 is the only `sink='validations'` caller today, but cairn/tools/base/validation.py:86 exposes `run_proof(path, sink='validations')` to anyone, and a provider does not know its consumers. (2) THE PRINT, in cli.py's `isolation_for` closure at :391-440, which already holds both the flag and the standing reading: when `--netns` is passed and the standing record disagrees, say so before the run, naming the proof and the standing reading. (3) THE SURFACE reports the refusal in its own line and the batch continues, matching the precedent already at cli.py:451 for the mirror guard. The docstring at cli.py:402 narrows with it: its stated reason — that an explicit ask is the only way to seal something the FIRST time — survives untouched, because a first seal has no standing record and the guard never sees it.
falsifier: DONE when (1) a run passing `--netns` whose standing record disagrees PRINTS the override before running, naming the proof and the standing reading; (2) persisting a measured seal over a standing `open` is refused at the store's write door unless a reason rides with it, and the reason lands permanently in the SURVIVING record's evidence — which is the only possible home for it, because the store replaces rather than appends and the superseded record does not survive to carry anything; (3) the refusal fires on EVERY persisting path, so a direct `isolation='netns'` call through cairn/tools/base/validation.py is covered too; (4) the surface reports the refusal in its own line and the batch continues; (5) the ordinary paths stay quiet — a first seal with no standing record, a plain `--seal` reproducing a standing `open` at `none`, and the pre-commit reseal ladder reproducing a standing reading all pass with no reason, because none of them converts anything. WRONG INTENT if the refusal merely relocates the silence: if the CLI starts auto-supplying its own reason so the guard passes on every run, the door is a turnstile and the 54 open readings convert exactly as they do today with a boilerplate sentence attached. The measurement is whether `open` readings disappear faster than reasons appear, not whether the guard exists.
measured_at_cast: 2026-09-10, all on fixtures under the live code at HEAD 57bd9cf. (a) THE SILENCE: a `cairn test --seal --netns` run over a fixture whose standing record was posed at `open` converted it to `sealed` and printed four lines containing neither the word 'override' nor the word 'standing' nor the prior reading — byte-identical in shape to a first seal. (b) THE PERMANENCE: a following plain `cairn test --seal` over the same fixture reproduced `netns`, so the deliberate `open` is gone from the record with nothing saying it ever stood. (c) THE MIRROR ALREADY HOLDS: firing `cairn.tools.base.validation.run_proof(path, sink='validations')` — which never forwards isolation, so it always runs at `none` — over a standing `sealed` raised SealDowngradeRefused, named both readings, offered `unsealing_because`, and left the standing record untouched. (d) THE POPULATION: across both roots, 219 validation trails — 159 standing at `sealed`, 54 at `open`, 6 carrying no seal key at all. All 54 are convertible today by one sweep. (e) `cli.py:379` reads `sink = 'validations' if args.seal else 'none'`, so `--netns` alone persists nothing and only the `--seal` combination reaches the door. (f) Validation records are written 0o444 at rest, which is why a fixture posing a standing seal must chmod and restore. (g) CORRECTED AFTER THE CAST, and it changes the watch: the tester's charter falsifier clause (6) says a validations file holding more than one record is itself a red, and the corpus agrees — all 219 files hold exactly ONE record, and `persist_validation` writes `[record]`. There is no trail and no superseded record. The first cut of this ticket's WATCHME proposed firing when an EARLIER record in a trail carried `open`; that reading is unbuildable because no earlier record exists. The watch is arithmetic against a baseline instead — see the corrected trigger.
traces_to: Law 7 (a record of truth may never collapse or quietly rewrite what was measured — and `open` records that nothing was measured, which is itself a reading); Law 3 (`open` is the recorded absence of a measurement, not a weak one, so overwriting it destroys the artifact that says so); Law 4 (the rule that a conversion carries a reason becomes the store's raise, not a sentence in a docstring); Law 1 (a reader who finds `sealed` where a deliberate `open` stood must re-derive why, from nothing).
known_hole_inherited_knowingly: The 54 standing `open` readings are NOT re-taken by this ticket. After it ships they still read `open`, and re-taking them becomes an explicit act that must carry a reason — which is the intended shape, not a gap. Their one-time re-take is separate work and is already carried in the queue. Second hole, named: the guard checks that a reason is PRESENT, never that it is a good one. A rote sentence passes. That is deliberate — a sieve measures and does not judge — and it is exactly what the WATCHME below is pointed at, by counting conversions rather than reading reasons.
from_idea: none, because this is a defect entering at the TICKET door (CLAUDE.md: if editing lines of code fixes it, it is a ticket). The origin is item B2 of the build queue in CairnCommons/slates/2026-09-10-the-gates-are-deterministic-and-one-hand-still-writes-crossings.json, whose wording this cast corrects against measurement — see `measured_at_cast` (c).
intent_berth: none, because a defect does not route through /intent. The origin record is the B2 line in CairnCommons/slates/2026-09-10-the-gates-are-deterministic-and-one-hand-still-writes-crossings.json, and the site is cairn/devices/tester/cli.py:434 whose measured behaviour is recorded in `measured_at_cast`.
cast_under: Item B2 of the build queue, pre-approved by Akien. Cast after measurement corrected its wording: the slate reads 'refuse a downgrade (netns->none) outright', and that half is already physics at validation_store.py:414 — fired and watched to refuse on 2026-09-10. The reachable defect is the mirror direction, open -> measured, which nothing guards. Carrying the slate's wording forward unmeasured would have re-derived a settled answer (Law 1).

watchme.trigger: TWO readings, files-and-a-function only, no device and no network. (1) THE BEHAVIOUR: call the store's guard predicate with a standing `open` and a measured incoming and assert it refuses — taken the way the sibling probe cairn/devices/tester/probes/a_first_seal_is_taken_under_the_seal.py takes its decision reading, so a refactor that moves the guard and loses it fires this rather than a source-grep a rename would fool. (2) THE ARITHMETIC: census the corpus for validations standing at `open`, and separately count validations standing at a MEASURED seal whose evidence carries the conversion reason. Fire when `open` readings have disappeared since arming faster than reasons have appeared for them — (54 - open_now) > reasoned_conversions. The arithmetic is necessary because the store REPLACES rather than appends: a converted record leaves no superseded `open` behind, so an unreasoned conversion is invisible in the record itself and visible only as a population that shrank with nothing accounting for it. KNOWN IMPRECISION, carried openly: a deleted or renamed validations file also shrinks the population and would fire this. That is acceptable — the probe deposits and pokes and carries no authority (Law 6), and a fire that turns out to be a rename is a cheap look, where a conversion that fires nothing is the false green this ticket exists against.
watchme.enough: 30 days elapsed since arming with the trigger not firing on any pulse. Thirty rather than seven for the sibling probe's recorded reason: the failure watched for is a HABIT re-forming — reaching for the flag to make a sweep uniform — and a habit needs enough voyages to form in. The elapsed clause is what stops the watch clearing on its first pulse, when the guard trivially holds because no traffic has run against it yet.
watchme.carrier: a verdict artifact against this ticket's falsifier, carrying the open-population arithmetic (baseline 54 at arming vs now), the reasoned-conversion count, the guard's live answer, and the by-verdict population beside it as context (159 sealed / 54 open / 6 no-seal-key, measured 2026-09-10)
